% hyperref, xr-hyper, then xr's old release, which \usepackage{xr}[=v5]
% loads. The old release's \externaldocument is the one used, with no URL.
% The page builds, and each reference prints as with the old release
% alone: from an .aux that LaTeX wrote under hyperref, its number, page,
% name, and \autoref as in the PDF, with no link; from an .aux that tex4ht
% wrote under hyperref, with its .xref, a link to that document's page,
% also through \externalcitedocument. The \@input{chap.aux} of
% test-xr/latex.aux is read beside this document, where no chap.aux is,
% so its label prints ??, as in the PDF.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{xr}[=v5]
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}
\externalcitedocument[H-]{test-xrboth/old-last}
\begin{document}
CaseJ \ref{X-ss}, page \pageref{X-front}, named \nameref{X-thm},
auto \autoref{X-thm}.

CaseK \ref{H-oss}.

Included \ref{X-c}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
